item.content:encoded:
The National Broadcasting Corporation [NBC] has given illegal squatters residing behind the 5 Mile headquarters in Port Moresby 21 days to leave the property or face eviction by police.

Managing Director Kora Nou made the announcement today following an alleged attack on the son of a senior NBC staff member over the weekend. The victim was taken to hospital and the family has reported the matter to police.

Mr Nou said NBC has started discussions with the Metropolitan Superintendent, and police officers will begin awareness with the squatters so they can voluntarily move out within the next 21 days.

“Failure to do so will result in NBC requesting the Courts and police to evict them.” Mr Nou said

He also called on the squatters to identify those responsible for the attack and hand them over to police for investigation.

“May I remind everyone that the officers of the NBC throughout the country provide an essential service to our people every day, on weekends, and public holidays.

“These officers and their families do not deserve such unprovoked physical attacks or daily intimidation as they carry out their work, especially within the confines of our institutional housing premises.

“Harassment, physical attacks and unruly drunken behaviour in the vicinity of our 5 Mile staff residences have also increased since more illegal settlers have moved in from eviction exercises in other parts of Port Moresby.

“We will work with the Courts, the police, and NCDC to immediately stop this, as well we remove the illegal squatters already there,” Mr Nou

Mr Nou said the eviction is also part of NBC's plans to develop the land. Funding has already been secured to build 38 new staff houses at the 5 Mile site, with construction expected to begin once a building permit is issued.

He said the land currently occupied by the illegal squatters is needed for the new housing project.

item.title: Governor Bird responds to Angoram boundary concern
item.description: East Sepik Governor Allan Bird has responded to concerns raised by communities in Angoram over the new Middle Sepik electoral boundary, saying the matter is now being addressed in consultation with relevant government agencies. item.content:encoded:
East Sepik Governor Allan Bird has responded to concerns raised by communities in Angoram over the new Middle Sepik electoral boundary, saying the matter is now being addressed in consultation with relevant government agencies.

The Governor's response was posted on his official Facebook page on Saturday, 1st August following concerns raised by the Kanda communities over the inclusion of parts of their customary land into the newly created Middle Sepik District.

In the Facebook statement, Governor Bird wrote, "The decision on the boundaries were made around 2021." He added that he had been informed a public consultation meeting was held at Sir Michael Somare Stadium in Wewak before the boundary decision was finalised.

According to the Governor, the East Sepik Provincial Government only received the final boundary decision in January this year. It was then that the province realised Angoram Station had been placed within the new district.

"We took a decision in 2023 to split Angoram Local Level Government into two so Angoram township will remain in Angoram District because ESPG has already decided to build the new district headquarters in Timbunke," the statement reads.

The Governor also acknowledged the legal challenges involved, stating, "We have been informed that we may be legally out of time." A technical team was established four weeks ago to work with the Department of Provincial and Local Government Affairs and other relevant agencies to resolve the boundary issues.

Governor Bird believes the situation could have been avoided had the Provincial Government been consulted during the 2021 boundary review.

"Had ESPG been consulted in 2021, the current issues would have been avoided," he wrote.

The Governor also assured the people of Angoram that they would be kept informed as discussions continue.

"I will inform our people in Angoram as to the outcomes of the consultations with relevant agencies once completed," Governor Bird wrote.

item.title: East Sepik holds tribute service for Rabaul boat tragedy victims
item.description: The East Sepik community gathered on Saturday to honor and remember the 27 lives lost in the recent tragic boat incident in Rabaul, East New Britain Province. A tribute mass was held on Saturday evening, 1st August 2026, at Marist beach, where men, women and children gathered to to pay their respects.
item.content:encoded:
The East Sepik community gathered on Saturday to honor and remember the 27 lives lost in the recent tragic boat incident in Rabaul, East New Britain Province.

A tribute mass was held on Saturday evening, 1st August 2026, at Marist beach, where men, women and children gathered to to pay their respects.

The service was conducted by Father Bernard Burite from Christ the King Church, Wiruwi Parish, and Reverend Robert Heni from Wewak United Church.

During the prayer for the victims, Reverend Heni reminded the congregation that life is uncertain and encouraged people to dedicate their lives to God.

“As we dedicate the 27 lives lost, please remember us who are alive on earth. May this tribute also remind those of us who are living that only God knows the future, and that we must always dedicate our lives to Him in everything we do,” Reverend Heni said.

Following the service, lanterns were raised into the night sky, while 27 wreaths were laid on the sea as a symbol of remembrance for each of the lives lost in the tragedy.

The solemn tribute brought together families, children and community members who gathered along the Wewak shoreline in prayer, reflection and solidarity with those affected by the incident.

The glowing lanterns above the shoreline and the wreaths placed on the sea marked a powerful moment of remembrance, as the East Sepik community joined the nation in mourning and honoring the victims of the Rabaul boat tragedy.

item.title: Ipatas is urging the national government to strengthen policing in Enga
item.description: Enga Governor Sir Peter Ipatas has called on the National Government to strengthen policing in the province, saying lasting peace depends on a well-resourced police force. His call comes as he backed the National Gun Amnesty Program, urging those in possession of illegal firearms to surrender them voluntarily.
item.content:encoded:
Enga Governor Sir Peter Ipatas has called on the National Government to strengthen policing in the province, saying lasting peace depends on a well-resourced police force.

His call comes as he backed the National Gun Amnesty Program, urging those in possession of illegal firearms to surrender them voluntarily.

Sir Peter said illegal guns have claimed many lives and destroyed schools, aid posts, churches and other government infrastructure across Enga.

"Illegal firearms must be surrendered voluntarily because they have destroyed so much state property and we have lost a lot of lives," he said.

While supporting the amnesty, Sir Peter said provincial governments had not been formally briefed on the National Executive Council's decision and called for clear guidelines on how the program will be implemented.

He questioned whether the initiative was solely a voluntary gun surrender or would include a gun buy-back scheme and economic support for those handing in weapons.

"As a government on the ground, we need clear direction on the program," he said.

The Governor said the Enga Provincial Government has consistently invested in policing and believes sustainable peace can only be achieved through stronger law enforcement.

He called on Police Minister Sir John Pundari to provide provincial governments with a clear implementation roadmap, including the program's objectives, funding, timeframe and any compensation arrangements.

Sir Peter also urged the Royal Papua New Guinea Constabulary to boost its presence in Enga by recruiting more police officers, providing additional vehicles, uniforms and equipment, and strengthening the Kumul 23 policing unit.

He further appealed for the immediate recruitment of three additional expatriate police officers to support Provincial Police Commander Chief Superintendent Steven Harris, noting that four positions are already funded by the Australian Government.

His comments come as Police Minister Sir John Pundari continues encouraging Papua New Guineans, particularly in Enga, to surrender illegal firearms ahead of the planned destruction of surrendered weapons on National Repentance Day on August 26.

item.title: One month on, Dr Nicole Haley yet to assume Electoral Commissioner role
item.description: It's been a month since the appointment of Electoral Commissioner Dr Nicole Haley to oversee election operations ahead of the 2027 general elections. Her appointment was made known on June 30.
item.content:encoded:
It's been a month since the appointment of Electoral Commissioner Dr Nicole Haley to oversee election operations ahead of the 2027 general elections.

Her appointment was made known on June 30.

However, questions are now being raised about when she will officially assume duties.

Several leaders have urged the Prime Minister and Chief Secretary to immediately ensure that Dr Nicole Haley is sworn into office.

Among them is Opposition Leader James Nomane, who said her delay in taking office is increasing the risks to election preparations and its conduct.

Chairman of the Special Parliamentary Committee on Elections Alan Bird said there are so many activities that need to be completed, such as updating the common roll, which is among the key focus of Dr Haley.

The office of the Prime Minister remains tight lipped on the reason for the delay.

But, according to government officials, there are statutory and administrative requirements that are yet to be completed before Dr Haley can formally take office.

One of these requirements is the salary and remuneration for her contract

item.title: Arson suspects involved in burning of Ramu police house appear in court
item.description: Two prime suspects allegedly responsible for the recent burning down of a police house and a private vehicle, belonging to the police officer whose house was torched to the ground at the Ramu Sugar Police Barracks, have appeared for mention before the Ramu District Court on two charges each for arson. The two were identified as 24- year- old Korago Sirimu, and his younger brother Taiman Sirimu, 18
item.content:encoded:
Two prime suspects allegedly responsible for the recent burning down of a police house and a private vehicle, belonging to the police officer whose house was torched to the ground at the Ramu Sugar Police Barracks, have appeared for mention before the Ramu District Court on two charges each for arson.

The two were identified as 24- year- old Korago Sirimu, and his younger brother Taiman Sirimu, 18 from Goiro Village in Naho/Rawa LLG, Raikos District.

They are both unemployed and reside at the Sakiko Care Centre near the Ramu Sugar township.

The two were part of a group of drunk men who were involved in illegal gambling. A fight broke out amongst the drunkard gamblers and when police arrived, Taiman fell in front of the police vehicle whilst trying to run away.

The police vehicle was falsely accused of running over Taiman killing him instantly. Officers who were on duty at that time assisted Taiman to the hospital where he was stabilised and received treatment for injuries he sustained during the drunken brawl.

However, in the process of doing this, the police officers and vehicle were stoned by the public.

Assuming that Taiman was dead, the public mobilised and marched to the township, stoned two police houses, and burnt down one plus all personal belongings, including the policeman’s private vehicle.

Meanwhile, 52 other suspects have been identified for malicious damages caused to one of the Treasury houses near the scene of the burnt down police house, break-ins, and stealing at the Kostko Investment Ltd Supermarket, and the Post Office boxes.

They were identified through CCTV footages retrieved from the shops as well as witnesses’ statements that were collected by the investigating team, led by First Constable Eliud Seipe.

Provincial Police Commander for Madang, Superintendent Robert Baim confirmed the two prime suspects have been moved to Lae for their own safety and will be detained at Buimo CS.

He said some of those involved are settlers who work as seasonal workers or labourers with the Ramu Agri- Industries Limited.

He added that Ramu town is generally peaceful, and such unruly behavior is not good for the public.

“Ramu Sugar just like any other towns, has people from all over Papua New Guinea working and living there. It’s a mixture of Papua New Guineans and the company should accommodate its seasonal workers properly instead of just allowing them to create settlements amongst the sugar fields and oil palm plantations.

“When people start coming up with all kinds of ideas, it is not good for law and order. It can create problems that are not good for the company and the township,” Superintendent Baim said.

item.title: More than 40,000 grade 12’s sit the written expression paper
item.description: Over 40,000 Grade 12 students across Papua New Guinea have begun sitting the first of this year’s major national examinations with the Written Expression Exam. In the Nation’s Capital, Gordons Secondary School is among 249 secondary schools participating nationwide, with over 300 Grade 12 students taking the exam.
item.content:encoded:
Over 40,000 Grade 12 students across Papua New Guinea have begun sitting the first of this year’s major national examinations with the Written Expression Exam.

In the Nation’s Capital, Gordons Secondary School is among 249 secondary schools participating nationwide, with over 300 Grade 12 students taking the exam.

Gordons Secondary School Principal George Kenega said the school is confident of a strong performance, with Language being one of the school’s strongest subjects.

Mr Kenega said 340 students were originally registered for the exam, with 331 currently sitting after 9 students withdrew.

“Right now, we have 340 registered, but 9 have withdrawn. So the actual number of students in the exam is 331. From the results that they got from the model exams, it was good. So, we expect our students to do well,” Mr. Kenega said.

He said most of the withdrawals were due to financial difficulties and personal problems, with some students transferring to other institutions including UNS.

A major challenge for the school is the lack of an assembly hall. Mr Kenega said the school has been waiting for approval to build a hall for 4 years.

As a result, exams are being conducted across nine separate classrooms.

“We have started at the old site, but it's taking too long. We have submitted the building design. To date, they have not given us approval to build a hall. Right now we are using nine exam rooms. If we had a hall, we would give everybody one area,” he said.

The Principal noted that a hall would make it easier to manage all students in one area and reduce logistical costs.

With the main Grade 10 and 12 examinations scheduled for November, Gordons Secondary has introduced daily remedial classes after normal lessons to further prepare students.

Three external invigilators are also overseeing the current exams to ensure integrity and prevent cheating.

Mr Kenega said the school remains committed to maintaining exam standards and supporting students despite the current space limitations.

The Written Expression Exam marks the start of the national examination period for Grade 12s, with further exams to follow in the coming months.

item.content:encoded:
‎The predicted onset of El Nino may lead to urban migration and social issues in the island communities of Lousiade in Samarai-Murua as the dry spell prolongs. ‎ As the prolonged dry spell continues, families in rural island communities in the Lousiade local level government may be forced to leave their homes and migrate to urban areas in search of food, water and better living conditions. ‎ ‎Lousiade LLG president Solomon Paulisbo said he dreads social issues could emerge once the full impact of the El Nino sets in Milne Bay.

“People will be forced to look for comforts in the urban areas, and they do that we are looking at social issues,” he said.

Paulisbo said they've established plans to respond to the El Nino effects but to date, they still haven't received any funding from the disaster relief components to implement their plans. ‎

item.title: Police launch manhunt for 16 escapees in Enga
item.description: A police operation is underway in Enga to recapture 16 remand prisoners who escaped from the Wabag Police Station lock-up early on Wednesday morning.

item.title: Police foil armed robbery along Sepik highway
item.description: Effective communication by police in East Sepik has led to the arrest of two armed men who were inside a PMV bus from Wewak that was on its way to Maprik.
